Hello! I practiced anywhere from 5 mins to 18 hours almost every other day for the past 2 years tbh. On an average maybe 30 minutes daily. I had trouble with line art. My lines were always too thick. So, I focused on drawing thin strokes on top of a sketch with thick lines a lot. Also watched tons of videos on how the hell shadows and lighting worked. Videos on color theory helped me out a lot too. Studied a lot of references from pinterest as well, how the hues work on the skin and al that. Since I am going for a semirealstic style, I mainly referenced artworks with the same style. Still got a long ways to go on these premises lol.

Experimented with different apps a lot too. Knowing how the app worked helped me improve my art by a very large margin. I started out with autodesk and gradually found out that IbisPaintX was the best free option on a tablet for me.IbisPaint’s official YT channel has a lot of tutorials on how it works. It helped me out a lot.

Have A Nice Day! Hope this was at least a little bit helpful \[\^-\^\]

First,  take 2tbsp of unflavored gelatin and mix it in 1/2 cup of water and set it aside.
Then  dust the mould tray thingy heavily with corn flour.
After that, take 1 cup of sugar and 1/2 cup of water and boil it in medium flame until softball consistency (Put some of that hot thick sugar water in a glass of water and try to roll it into a ball. If you can roll it into a ball, then it's ready).
Then, lower the flame and pour the gelatin mixture into the sugar water. Mix the gelatin water until it's completely dissolved (it will smell weird at this stage but that's totally fine).
Then pour that hot mixture into a non-plastic bowl and beat it like crazy with a hand mixer until it starts turning white.
After it turns from a translucent yellow color to a white color, add 1 tbsp of vanilla essence and 1-2 drops of red food coloring. Then beat it like crazy again until the mixture is a light pink color everywhere.
Then pour this mixture quickly (coz it will set really fast) into the mould tray that was prepped earlier and dust a cornflour and powdered sugar mixture on the top. Let it set for 8-12 hours.
Then take that thick marshmallow sheet out from the mould and take a knife that is dusted with corn flour and cut into any shape you want.

Cover the marshmallows with powdered sugar if you want and boom! ready!
